$comment: Accepted occurrences of the settled-read-state shapes (`silent-guard`: a `useQuery` destructured for `data` with no outcome field plus an `if (!data) return null`; `default-literal`: `data: x = []` bound at the destructure, whose collapse is invisible at every use site downstream) (see scripts/check-settled-read-states.mjs and docs/adr/0010-settled-read-states.md). Each entry states why this component's absence — or its empty default — cannot be mistaken for an all-clear. The list may only SHRINK: adding an entry admits new debt and needs the reason to hold up in review; a stale entry fails the gate so a fix must delete its line. Do not add a component that carries a warning, a safety fact, or a count a reader would act on.

accepted.components/HouseholdSwitcher.tsx::member: A navigation control, not a report. Its absence removes the ability to switch households; it does not assert anything about the household's plants, and a user who cannot see the switcher has not been told that everything is fine.
accepted.features/dashboard/YearInReviewCard.tsx:: A retrospective recap of a year already lived. It carries no warning and nothing time-sensitive, and the component documents hiding rather than drawing empty bars. A missing recap makes no claim about today.
accepted.features/plants/PhotoTimeline.tsx::photo: Decorative history. The plant's current photo is rendered by PlantImage regardless, so a missing strip removes no fact from the page, and the component already documents hiding at one photo or fewer.
accepted.features/plants/SuggestedCareCard.tsx::d: A pre-save suggestion on the AddPlant form, adjacent to the fields it would fill. Absence means no suggestion was offered, which is what the user sees either way; the plant's real schedule is created explicitly afterwards. Pet toxicity on this same form is NOT here: PetToxicityNote carries it on its own read, precisely because that one is a safety fact.
accepted.features/plants/AddPlantPage.tsx::taskTe: A task-template suggestion on the AddPlant form. `suggestTaskTemplate` is the only reader, and an empty list means no template is pre-selected — which is what the user sees when no template matches the species either. The plant's real schedule is created explicitly on the next step, so absence offers nothing rather than asserting anything. Same reasoning as SuggestedCareCard on the same form; pet toxicity is deliberately NOT on this footing, because that one is a safety fact.
